answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the mirror schedule in the jetty ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the timber checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 2 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Running 98 aliases therefore means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest agents do not face at scale. That is 26 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
